name: Review a Paper
description: Critical review of methodology, statistical rigor, limitations, and constructive feedback
prompt:
Prepare an evidence-bounded peer-review draft of the uploaded paper. Treat unpublished material as confidential and use the peer-review skill's intake and safety requirements before analysis: if authorization to use AI, the venue's AI/confidentiality policy, a conflict of interest, or the requested review scope is unclear, ask only the minimum blocking questions together via the interview tool before reading or quoting the manuscript. Do not expose confidential manuscript text or distinctive details to web searches or other external services.

Work in this order:
1. Establish the review context, materials available, intended scope, and any competence limits. If no special focus is requested, perform a comprehensive review.
2. Give a short, neutral study map: research question, design, population or system, intervention or exposure, comparator, outcomes, and principal claims. Distinguish information that is not reported from information that is methodologically inadequate.
3. Assess claim-evidence alignment. For each central claim, identify the supporting result, figure, table, or analysis and judge whether the direction, magnitude, uncertainty, population, and causal language are supported.
4. Evaluate study design and methods: sampling, controls, randomization or masking where applicable, unit of analysis, confounding and bias, measurement validity, sample-size or precision rationale, missing data, and fit to the relevant reporting guideline.
5. Evaluate statistics: test-model fit, assumptions, multiplicity and prespecification, effect sizes, confidence or credible intervals, exact denominators, robustness or sensitivity analyses, and whether interpretation exceeds the design.
6. Review reproducibility and transparency, including protocol or registration consistency, data and code availability, software and parameter reporting, ethics approvals, consent, funding, conflicts, and contribution statements where applicable.
7. Check every figure, table, and citation that bears on a central conclusion for consistency with the text, readable labeling, denominators, units, uncertainty, and adequate context.
8. Draft the review as: review scope and limits; concise summary; key strengths; major comments; minor comments; and an overall evidence assessment. Each comment must include the manuscript location, the observation, why it matters, and a specific proportionate action. Prioritize threats to validity and claim support over stylistic preferences. Do not recommend acceptance or rejection unless the user explicitly requests it and the venue permits it; keep any confidential editor-only comments separate from comments to authors.

Ground every statement in the supplied materials and cite exact section, page, figure, table, or line locations when available. Never invent quotations, data, analyses, citations, manuscript locations, or author intentions. State uncertainty, flag specialist-review needs, and avoid requesting new experiments unless they are necessary to support a central claim; suggest clarification, reanalysis, narrower claims, or added limitation language when sufficient. Label the result as a working draft requiring human verification. Save it as a clearly named Markdown file in the sandbox, then give a brief chat summary of the most consequential strengths, concerns, unresolved questions, and saved path.
